name: Lachlan Giles Body Lock Passing System
description: A companion to Lachlan Giles’s The Body Lock Pass, using its advertised stages and narrated rolling to distinguish torso connection from clearing the legs.
summary: Separate securing the body lock, clearing the knee line and finishing the pass in Lachlan Giles’s focused passing study.
overview: The Body Lock Pass by Lachlan Giles concentrates on one passing family across six volumes. Its official description separates entry, controlling the opponent, knee clearance and finishing, with narrated rolling. Use those distinctions to locate a sticking point instead of treating a secure lock as a completed pass.

flashcards.question: Why does connecting the hands in the public Lachlan Giles body-lock explanation not yet complete the pass?
flashcards.answer: The written explanation still has the passer clear the first knee and then free the remaining leg. Securing the torso connection and clearing the legs are separate events.

flashcards.question: In the public explanation of Lachlan Giles’s body-lock pass, why distinguish the first knee clearance from the final leg clearance?
flashcards.answer: After the first knee clears, the description still accounts for the other leg being held in half guard. Clearing one knee therefore does not establish that both legs are free.
flashcards.answer_line: One leg may remain in half guard

start_here.title: Locate the leg barrier after the hands connect
start_here.task: Read the linked public explanation, The Body Lock Pass, with Lachlan Giles. Mark the point where the hands connect, where the first knee clears, and where the remaining leg is freed. Compare those distinct events with your own study notes. The written explanation supplies the observation task; the embedded video has not been reviewed here.
